title: Array representation of a perfect binary tree
summary: Store a perfect binary tree in level order in a zero-based array, and locate left and right children with index formulas 2i+1 and 2i+2.
context: A 4-level perfect binary tree has 15 nodes with values 1 through 15 in level order (root 1 on level 1, 2 and 3 on level 2, 4 through 7 on level 3, and leaf nodes 8 through 15 on level 4), stored sequentially at array indices 0 through 14. The table below lists every node's index and its left and right child positions.
result: Index formulas replace child pointers, but array bounds must still be checked on access: in this figure, indices 7 through 14 (nodes 8 through 15) are leaf nodes, so their computed child positions 15 through 30 are all out of bounds, indicating no children.

frames.title: Array representation of a perfect binary tree
frames.explanation: Substitute the array index i—not the node value—into the formulas. For example, node 6 is at index 5, so its left and right children are at index 11 (value 12) and index 12 (value 13).
